title: Under the Wave off Kanagawa (The Great Wave)
description: A world-renowned woodblock print depicting towering cresting waves framing Mount Fuji in the background. Part of the 'Thirty-Six Views of Mount Fuji' series.
creator: Katsushika Hokusai (Japanese, 1760–1849)
depicted_location: Off the coast of Kanagawa Prefecture overlooking Mount Fuji, Japan
current_collection: Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York, NY
attribution: Katsushika Hokusai / The Metropolitan Museum of Art (Open Access)

verified_facts.fact_text: Engraved and printed in the commercial workshops of Edo using polychrome woodblock print (nishiki-e) techniques.
verified_facts.source_citation: Metropolitan Museum Department of Asian Art, Accession No. JP1847

verified_facts.fact_text: Utilized synthetic Prussian Blue (Berlin blue) imported via Nagasaki, contrasting with traditional indigo.
verified_facts.source_citation: Tokyo National Museum Archival Pigment Analysis (2019)

verified_facts.fact_text: The boats depicted are oshiokuri-bune, swift cargo transport vessels navigating Edo Bay toward the Nihonbashi fish markets.

relations.notes: Master ukiyo-e painter and printmaker active during the late Edo period.
Capital seat of the Tokugawa Shogunate and print publishing hub.
Genre of Japanese art flourishing from the 17th through 19th centuries.
Accession 1936 / JP1847, H. O. Havemeyer Collection.
Contemporary Edo woodblock print documenting metropolitan urban life.

title: Night View of Saruwaka-machi (Saruwaka-chō yoru no kei)
description: Full moon casting dramatic human shadows along Saruwaka-chō, the designated theater district of Edo established following the 1841 Tenpō reforms.
source_name: Brooklyn Museum / Metropolitan Museum of Art
creator: Utagawa Hiroshige (Japanese, 1797–1858)
attribution: Utagawa Hiroshige / Brooklyn Museum Open Access

verified_facts.fact_text: Plate 90 in the iconic series 'One Hundred Famous Views of Edo' (Meisho Edo Hyakkei).
verified_facts.source_citation: Brooklyn Museum Asian Art Collection Records, 30.1478.90

verified_facts.fact_text: Saruwaka-chō was constructed in Asakusa in 1842 when the Kabuki theaters (Ichimura-za, Nakamura-za, Morita-za) were forcibly relocated outside inner Edo.
verified_facts.source_citation: Tokyo Metropolitan Archives Historical Cartography Division

relations.notes: Leading landscape printmaker of the Utagawa school.
Northern entertainment hub and historic theater quarter of Edo.
Shared printmaking tradition and commercial publishing network with Hokusai.
Exemplary 19th-century Japanese landscape woodblock print.

title: The Rosetta Stone
description: Fragment of a granodiorite stele inscribed with three versions of a decree issued in Memphis by King Ptolemy V Epiphanes, essential in deciphering ancient Egyptian hieroglyphs.
creator: Priests of Memphis (Decree authority)
discovery_location: Fort Julien near Rashid (Rosetta), Nile Delta, Egypt
current_collection: The British Museum, London, United Kingdom
attribution: The Trustees of the British Museum / Wikimedia Commons (Public Photograph)

verified_facts.fact_text: Contains parallel inscriptions in Egyptian hieroglyphs (sacred script), Demotic (civilian cursive), and Ancient Greek (administrative).
verified_facts.source_citation: British Museum Department of Egypt and Sudan, Object EA24

verified_facts.fact_text: Uncovered in July 1799 by French engineering officer Pierre-François Bouchard during Napoleon's Egyptian Expedition at Fort Julien.
verified_facts.source_citation: Institut d'Égypte Bulletin and Field Records (1799)

verified_facts.fact_text: Key phonetic breakthrough achieved by Jean-François Champollion in Paris in 1822 based on cartouches of Ptolemy and Cleopatra.
verified_facts.source_citation: Lettre à M. Dacier relative à l'alphabet des hiéroglyphes phonétiques (1822)

relations.notes: Port city at the western mouth of the Nile River where Fort Julien stood.
Ancient capital of Lower Egypt where the decree was synodically ratified.
Bilingual civic stele traditions integrating Hellenistic ruler cults and Pharaonic religion.
Acquired under the 1801 Treaty of Alexandria, on display since 1802.
Fellow landmark artifact of Ancient Egyptian civilization and monumental archaeology.

title: Bust of Nefertiti
description: Painted stucco-coated limestone bust of Nefertiti, the Great Royal Wife of Pharaoh Akhenaten, celebrated for its masterly proportional symmetry and preservation of Amarna-period royal portraiture.
source_name: Ägyptisches Museum und Papyrussammlung / Staatliche Museen zu Berlin
creator: Thutmose (Royal Master Sculptor)
discovery_location: Workshop of Sculptor Thutmose (Grid P 47.1-3), Tell el-Amarna, Minya Governorate, Egypt
rights_statement: Public Domain (3D and Photographic Reproductions under CC licenses)
attribution: Staatliche Museen zu Berlin / Philip Pikart (Wikimedia CC BY-SA 3.0)

verified_facts.fact_text: Discovered on 6 December 1912 during excavations of the German Oriental Society (Deutsche Orient-Gesellschaft) led by Ludwig Borchardt.
verified_facts.source_citation: Borchardt Excavation Journal, Tagebuch der Grabung in Tell el-Amarna (1912)

verified_facts.fact_text: Consists of a limestone core covered with varied thickness layers of painted stucco; right eye contains inserted rock crystal iris.
verified_facts.source_citation: CT Scan Analysis, Imaging Science & Neues Museum Conservation Report (2009)

relations.notes: Chief royal sculptor during the reign of Akhenaten at Akhetaten.
New religious capital founded on the east bank of the Nile by Akhenaten.
Distinctive expressive artistic style breaking from traditional rigid Egyptian canons.
Inventarnummer 21834, exhibited in the North Dome Room.
Ancient Egyptian archaeological landmark reflecting dynastic and Hellenistic transitions.

title: The Starry Night
description: Oil on canvas depicting the view from the east-facing window of the Saint-Paul-de-Mausole monastery bedroom, with an idealized village, swirling celestial sky, and prominent cypress tree.
creator: Vincent van Gogh (Dutch, 1853–1890)
depicted_location: Alpilles mountain range and view outside Saint-Paul Asylum, Saint-Rémy-de-Provence, France
current_collection: The Museum of Modern Art, New York, NY
attribution: Vincent van Gogh / Museum of Modern Art / Google Art Project

verified_facts.fact_text: Painted during Van Gogh's convalescence at the Saint-Paul-de-Mausole asylum in Saint-Rémy-de-Provence following his departure from Arles.
verified_facts.source_citation: Van Gogh Letters Project, Letter 779 to Theo van Gogh (ca. 2 June 1889)

verified_facts.fact_text: Astronomical historical reconstruction confirms the bright morning star depicted is Venus, visible in Provence at dawn in June 1889.
verified_facts.source_citation: Southwest Texas State University Astronomical Analysis of Van Gogh Works (Albert Boime, 1984)

relations.notes: Pioneering post-impressionist master whose expressive color reshaped modern painting.
Provençal commune in the foothills of the Alpilles.
Late 19th-century French movement emphasizing emotional resonance and structural color.
Acquired through the Lillie P. Bliss Bequest, 1941.

title: Kneeling Archer (Terracotta Army)
description: Life-sized terracotta sculpture of an armored kneeling crossbow archer, wearing a square-toed shoe and topknot hairstyle, excavated from Pit 2 of the Qin Shi Huang Mausoleum.
creator: Qin Imperial Workshop Artisans
discovery_location: Pit 2, Emperor Qinshihuang Mausoleum, Lintong District, Xi'an, Shaanxi, China
current_collection: Emperor Qinshihuang's Mausoleum Site Museum, Xi'an, China
rights_statement: UNESCO World Heritage Site / Cultural Relics Protection Law of PRC
attribution: Emperor Qinshihuang's Mausoleum Site Museum / Maros M r a z (Wikimedia CC BY-SA 3.0)

verified_facts.fact_text: Unearthed in March 1974 by local farmers drilling wells east of Mount Li in Lintong, Xi'an.
verified_facts.source_citation: Shaanxi Provincial Institute of Archaeology Excavation Monograph (1975)

verified_facts.fact_text: Originally coated with egg-based tempera over Chinese purple (barium copper silicate) and cinnabar, which oxidizes rapidly upon exposure to air.
verified_facts.source_citation: Bavarian State Conservation Office and Shaanxi Cultural Heritage Joint Research (2001)

relations.notes: Ancient capital of the Qin Empire and eastern terminus of the historic Silk Road.
Massive state-directed artisanal production for imperial subterranean protection.
Designated UNESCO World Heritage Site No. 441 in 1987.

title: The Intihuatana Stone of Machu Picchu
description: Monolithic carved granodiorite outcrop located at the highest point of the Sacred Plaza of Machu Picchu, functioning as a ritual calendar and solar observatory.
source_name: UNESCO World Heritage Centre & Ministry of Culture of Peru
creator: Inca Royal Stonemasons (Reign of Pachacuti Inca Yupanqui)
creation_location: Machu Picchu, Urubamba Province, Cusco Region, Peru
discovery_location: Sacred Plaza, Machu Picchu, Cusco Region, Peru
current_collection: In situ, Historic Sanctuary of Machu Picchu, Peru
rights_statement: World Heritage Monument / National Cultural Heritage of Peru

verified_facts.fact_text: The four corners of the carved pillar point toward the four cardinal directions; during the equinoxes, the sun sits directly above the pillar creating virtually no shadow.
verified_facts.source_citation: Archaeoastronomy Journal of the Center for Archaeoastronomy (Bingham Archival Review)

verified_facts.fact_text: Carved directly into the living granite bedrock summit rather than assembled from quarried blocks, an exemplar of Inca ashlar harmony with sacred landscapes (huacas).
verified_facts.source_citation: INC Cusco Geological and Architectural Survey (2000)

relations.notes: 15th-century Inca royal estate nestled between Andean peaks above the Urubamba River.
Sacred landscape integration where rocks embody spiritual vitality (huaca).

relations.target_name: Historic Sanctuary of Machu Picchu (In Situ)
relations.notes: Preserved in its original architectural orientation on the pyramid ridge.

creator: Unknown artisan
